# `sourcepsd_bins`

the power of a recording's sources at every Welch bin of a band, through an inverse kernel.

Version 1, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run sourcepsd_bins --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run sourcepsd_bins --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run sourcepsd_bins --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest --all --kernel NAME --bands '["8-12 Hz","13-30 Hz"]' --band_names '["alpha","beta"]' --band_name alpha
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `recording` | field recording, each true, where {"name": "$recording"} | yes |
| `kernel` | operator inverse kernel, from recording.manifold.0, where {"name": "$kernel"} | yes |
| `bad` | selection spans, manifold recording.time, where {"name": "{recording}_bad_segments"}, required false | no |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `recording` | `--recording` | `none` | - |  | the recording's name, or none: every recording of the subject, one run each |
| `kernel` | `--kernel` | `required` | - |  | the inverse kernel's name: which kernel the sources are read through is the caller's choice |
| `bands` | `--bands` | `required` | Hz |  | the band set select.bands makes: a list of quantities in Hz ("8-12 Hz"), each the span [lo, hi) of the frequency line (the caller's choice, no default) |
| `band_names` | `--band-names` | none | - |  | one name per band of the set; none: the range, e.g. 8-12 |
| `band_name` | `--band-name` | `required` | - |  | the member of the band set to read bin by bin: its name (the Welch bins from its lo to its hi inclusive are kept) |
| `segment_seconds` | `--segment-seconds` | `4.0` | s |  | the segment's length in seconds (under segment_rule tile it snaps to the nearest 2^k samples) |
| `segment_samples` | `--segment-samples` | none | samples |  | the segment's length in samples (wins over segment_seconds); null: from segment_seconds |
| `segment_rule` | `--segment-rule` | `tile` | - | tile, round, even | how the segment's length becomes samples: tile \| round \| even |
| `overlap` | `--overlap` | `0.5` | fraction |  | the fraction of a segment shared with the next, in [0, 1) |
| `window` | `--window` | `hamming` | - | hann, hamming, blackman, rectangular | the taper of each segment |
| `periodic` | `--periodic` | false | - |  | the DFT-even form of the window rather than the symmetric one |
| `detrend` | `--detrend` | `constant` | - | none, constant, linear | what is removed from each segment before windowing |
| `scaling` | `--scaling` | `density` | - | density, spectrum, chain | density = power per Hz \| spectrum = power \| chain = per sample, per bin |
| `bad_segments` | `--bad-segments` | `exclude` | - | exclude, ignore | exclude = a segment touching one of the recording's bad segments is left out \| ignore = every segment is kept |

## Presets

`--set <preset>` sets the parameters below at once; a parameter given by name wins over the preset.

| preset | sets |
|---|---|
| `tiles` | segment_rule=tile |
| `brainstorm` | segment_rule=round, window=hamming, periodic=false, detrend=constant, scaling=density |
| `scipy` | segment_rule=round, window=hann, periodic=true, detrend=constant, scaling=density |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | [`select.bands`](../nodes.md) |  | rule=frequency, bands=$bands, names=$band_names | bands |
| chunks over `recording` | [`meeg.source_bins`](../nodes.md) | x=recording, kernel=kernel, exclude=bad, bands=bands | band=$band_name, segment_seconds=$segment_seconds, segment_samples=$segment_samples, segment_rule=$segment_rule, overlap=$overlap, window=$window, periodic=$periodic, detrend=$detrend, scaling=$scaling, bad_segments=$bad_segments | bins |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `bins` | kind statistic, name {recording}_{kernel}_psd_$band_name_bins, of recording, axes [{"name": "vertex", "on": "kernel.to"}, {"name": "frequency", "line": "{recording}_{kernel}_$band_name_bins_freq"}], partition {"tiling": "{recording}_{kernel}_psd_$band_name_bins_segments", "on": "recording.time"} |

## Notes from the definition

```text
THE POWER OF A RECORDING'S SOURCES, BIN BY BIN WITHIN ONE BAND (a statistic; sourcepsd's `--resolve bins`): the frequency partition's members are the Welch bins from lo to hi Hz
inclusive, nothing reduced over frequency, so each source keeps its spectrum within the band. The kernel is applied to each segment's Fourier coefficients and |K X|^2 summed per source
per bin (nxr::signal::spectral::LinearWelch): the source side holds sources x bins, never the channels^2 x bins of the cross-spectrum route; the same numbers to rounding. `kernel` and the band set are
the caller's choice (no default); the set is a selection made first (select.bands) and the node reads the band from it through an edge. The band statistic of `run sourcepsd` is the mean of these bins. One run a band; stored: the statistic `<recording>_<kernel>_psd_<band>_bins`
(measure power_density or power, by welch, OF the recording; axes vertex (the kernel's target) x frequency, the frequency line the band's bins), and its segment partition `<name>_segments`.
It cannot resolve: what the kernel cannot (a minimum-norm kernel spreads each source over its neighbours); a bin is one Welch bin, its width the segment's 1 / length.

  nxr-neuro run sourcepsd_bins --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest --all --kernel NAME --bands '["8-12 Hz","13-30 Hz"]' --band_names '["alpha","beta"]' --band_name alpha
```
